grammar.content.2: Before learning grammar, you need to be able to read the Japanese that appears throughout the course.
grammar.content.8: Learn to read before starting to ‘translate’
grammar.content.9: This topic lays the foundation for the whole course. The goal is not to memorize words yet, but to recognize Japanese sounds and understand how they are represented in writing.
grammar.content.10:
ひらがな
→
カタカナ
→
漢字
grammar.content.12: You should be able to read kana without constantly relying on romaji
grammar.content.13: You do not need to read quickly yet. What matters is recognizing the symbols, pronouncing syllables and moving on to Topic 01 without writing becoming a barrier.
grammar.content.18: An introduction to the three systems you will see in Japanese: hiragana, katakana and kanji. You will not study kanji here yet; you will only learn what each system is used for.
grammar.content.21: You will learn the basic hiragana syllables and associate them directly with their sounds, without relying on romaji.
grammar.content.22: あ aか kaさ saた taな na
grammar.content.24: You will see how small marks transform certain sounds: か → が, さ → ざ, は → ば / ぱ.
grammar.content.25: か → がは → ばは → ぱ
grammar.content.27: An introduction to combinations with small ゃ・ゅ・ょ. You will learn to read sounds such as きゃ, しゅ or ちょ.
grammar.content.28: きゃ kyaしゅ shuちょ cho
grammar.content.30: Small っ marks a brief pause and doubles the following consonant. It is essential for distinguishing words correctly.
grammar.content.33: You will learn how vowel sounds are lengthened in hiragana and katakana. Vowel length can change how a word is recognized.
grammar.content.36: You will learn the second Japanese syllabary, used mainly for loanwords, foreign names, onomatopoeia and certain forms of emphasis.
grammar.content.39: Before starting Topic 01, you will learn three important pronunciation exceptions when these kana function as particles.
grammar.content.48: Which writing system is mainly being used?
grammar.content.52: Correct. テレビ is written in katakana, which is commonly used for loanwords.
grammar.content.53: Notice the angular shapes of the characters. テレビ is written in katakana.
grammar.content.54: Understand what hiragana, katakana and kanji are used for before starting to study them.
grammar.content.55: Used for Japanese words, endings and many grammatical elements.
grammar.content.56: Mainly used for foreign words, foreign names, onomatopoeia and certain forms of emphasis.
grammar.content.57: Characters with meaning. In this topic you will only learn to recognize their existence; you will not study them yet.
grammar.content.58: You do not need to learn kanji yet. The goal is to recognize which system you are looking at.
grammar.content.61: This subtopic has a brief explanation and one main exercise. Cumulative practice comes later.
grammar.content.63: Read kana without constantly relying on romaji before starting the grammar in Topic 01.
grammar.content.72: The correct answer is ‘ki’. き belongs to the か・き・く・け・こ row.
grammar.content.73: Start associating each hiragana symbol directly with its sound.
grammar.content.75: They are the foundation of the syllabary.
grammar.content.77: Most symbols combine a consonant with a vowel.
grammar.content.79: We want to move from seeing a symbol to recognizing its sound without relying on romaji.
grammar.content.80: Romaji is a temporary aid. You should gradually stop needing it.
grammar.content.82: Add dakuten to か. What do you get?
grammar.content.89: Dakuten changes か (ka) into が (ga).
grammar.content.90: Recognize how small marks change the sounds of certain kana.
grammar.content.92: Changes certain voiceless sounds into voiced sounds.
grammar.content.94: The same pattern affects several rows.
grammar.content.96: Used in the は row to create sounds with p.
grammar.content.97: The marks ゛ and ゜ change the sound even though the base kana remains recognizable.
grammar.content.106: The ゃ is small, so it combines with き: きゃ = kya.
grammar.content.107: Learn to read combinations with small ゃ・ゅ・ょ.
grammar.content.109: Small ゃ・ゅ・ょ combine with the preceding kana.
grammar.content.111: The combination is pronounced as one unit.
grammar.content.113: きや and きゃ do not represent the same thing.
grammar.content.114: When ゃ・ゅ・ょ are small, they form a combined sound with the preceding kana.
grammar.content.116: Are these two forms pronounced the same way?
grammar.content.120: Correct. They are pronounced differently: きって contains a brief pause before て.
grammar.content.121: No. Small っ introduces a pause and doubles the following consonant.
grammar.content.122: Understand that small っ introduces a brief pause and affects the following consonant.
grammar.content.124: Small っ marks a very short interruption before the next sound.
grammar.content.126: In romaji it is usually represented by doubling the following consonant.
grammar.content.128: The presence of っ is not decorative.
grammar.content.129: Small っ must be heard and read: it changes the rhythm and can change the word.
grammar.content.131: Which of these forms contains a long vowel?
grammar.content.135: Correct. おばあさん contains a long vowel in ああ.
grammar.content.136: The form with a long vowel is おばあさん: the second あ lengthens the sound.
grammar.content.137: Recognize that vowel length is part of pronunciation.
grammar.content.139: A short vowel and a long vowel can distinguish words.
grammar.content.141: The vowel can be lengthened by adding another vowel.
grammar.content.143: The long mark ー is often used.
grammar.content.144: Do not ignore long vowels. They are part of the word and must be pronounced.
grammar.content.151: Correct. ア and あ represent the sound “a”.
grammar.content.152: The hiragana equivalent of ア is あ.
grammar.content.153: Recognize the second syllabary and connect it with the sounds you already know.
grammar.content.155: Hiragana and katakana represent essentially the same basic sounds.
grammar.content.157: Katakana appears often in words of foreign origin.
grammar.content.159: We also want to recognize katakana without relying on romaji.
grammar.content.160: Katakana is not another language: it is another system for representing Japanese sounds.
grammar.content.162: How is は pronounced in this sentence?
grammar.content.163: わたし は がくせいです。
grammar.content.168: Correct. Here は acts as a particle, so it is pronounced “wa”.
grammar.content.169: In this sentence は acts as a particle. It is pronounced “wa”.
grammar.content.170: Learn three pronunciation exceptions before starting the grammar in Topic 01.
grammar.content.172: It is normally read ha, but as a particle it is pronounced wa.
grammar.content.174: It is normally read he, but as a particle it is pronounced e.
grammar.content.176: When it acts as a particle, it is usually pronounced o.
grammar.content.177: You do not need to master what these particles do yet. Just recognize their special pronunciation in context.
grammar.content.180: You will no longer know in advance which subtopic is being tested. The idea is to check whether you recognize the patterns without relying on the lesson order.
grammar.content.188: Each round shuffles the questions and options so you learn the concept, not a fixed position.
grammar.content.193: Dakuten, combined sounds and small っ.
grammar.content.197: Special pronunciation of は・へ・を.
grammar.content.201: Which writing system is mainly used?
grammar.content.202: テレビ is written in katakana, common in many words of foreign origin.
grammar.content.224: The small ゅ combines with し: しゅ = “shu”.
grammar.content.227: Are they pronounced exactly the same?
grammar.content.229: No. さっか contains a brief pause produced by the small っ.
grammar.content.232: Which contains a long vowel marked with ー?
grammar.content.236: コーヒー contains the mark ー, which lengthens the vowel.
grammar.content.243: カ and か represent the sound “ka”.
grammar.content.246: Here は acts as a particle, so it is pronounced “wa”.
grammar.content.254: きょ contains a small ょ combined with き.
grammar.content.257: スーパー へ いきます。
grammar.content.258: スーパー is in hiragana
grammar.content.259: へ is pronounced “he” as a particle
grammar.content.260: スーパー contains a long vowel and へ is pronounced “e” as a particle
grammar.content.262: スーパー is in katakana and contains ー. Also, へ as a particle is pronounced “e”.
grammar.content.264: Build your first sentences in Japanese and learn to introduce, identify and ask questions.
grammar.content.268: Build simple sentences with nouns and understand how topic, identification and questions work.
grammar.content.272: You should be able to introduce yourself, identify objects and ask basic nominal questions without relying on romaji.
grammar.content.273: The next topic will build on this knowledge, so the progression avoids introducing structures that have not been explained yet.
grammar.content.278: General word order in a Japanese sentence
grammar.content.279: Japanese usually places the main information at the end. Here we introduce the idea of topic + information, without trying to translate word for word.
grammar.content.280: わたし は カルロス ですA は B です
grammar.content.282: Learn the polite copula です to say that something 'is' or identify it in basic sentences.
grammar.content.283: わたしはカルロスです。これはほんです。
grammar.content.284: Introduces the plain version of the copula. The aim is not to use it everywhere yet, but to recognize the relationship between です and だ.
grammar.content.287: The particle は marks what we are talking about. It is introduced as a topic marker, not as a literal translation of 'is'.
grammar.content.288: わたしはがくせいです。これはほんです。
grammar.content.290: Learn to turn a polite sentence into a question by adding か at the end.
grammar.content.291: がくせいです。がくせいですか。
grammar.content.293: Use も to show that something shares the same information as an item already mentioned.
grammar.content.294: わたしもがくせいです。これもほんです。
grammar.content.296: The particle の connects two nouns. It can express possession, belonging, origin or a relationship.
grammar.content.297: わたしのほんにほんのアニメ
grammar.content.299: Learn to point to things depending on whether they are near the speaker, near the listener or far from both.
grammar.content.300: これはなんですか。それはほんです。
grammar.content.302: These forms directly accompany a noun. They cannot appear alone.
grammar.content.303: このほんそのかばんあのひと
grammar.content.304: ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ
grammar.content.305: Introduces place demonstratives and the basic question 'where?'.
grammar.content.308: Learn to negate nominal sentences with じゃないです / ではありません, also recognizing the plain form じゃない.
grammar.content.309: がくせいじゃないです。せんせいではありません。
grammar.content.311: Learn to talk about past nominal states with でした and だった.
grammar.content.312: がくせいでした。やすみだった。
grammar.content.314: Completes the basic copula system with じゃなかったです / ではありませんでした.
grammar.content.315: がくせいじゃなかったです。せんせいではありませんでした。
grammar.content.322: わたしはがくせいです。
grammar.content.327: Understand that Japanese organizes information differently from Spanish and that the verb or copula usually ends the sentence.
grammar.content.333: In basic nominal sentences, です usually ends the sentence.
grammar.content.336: We now start working with structures we will reuse throughout N5.
grammar.content.338: Build and understand basic nominal sentences without relying on word-for-word translations.
grammar.content.343: Correct. わたしはがくせいです。
grammar.content.344: The sentence needs the polite ending です.
grammar.content.345: Learn to identify or describe something politely using です.
grammar.content.347: です is used to end many nominal sentences politely.
grammar.content.349: It lets you say what something is or who someone is.
grammar.content.350: It is not a verb identical to “be”
grammar.content.351: Its function resembles “be”, but it should not be translated mechanically.
grammar.content.352: At this level, use it as a polite ending for sentences with nouns and な-adjectives.
grammar.content.359: Correct. がくせいだ is the plain form.
grammar.content.360: The corresponding plain copula here is だ.
grammar.content.361: Recognize だ as the plain form of the copula in nominal sentences.
grammar.content.363: だ is a plain form that contrasts with the polite register of です.
grammar.content.365: It does not express a different meaning; it mainly changes the register.
grammar.content.367: At first, recognizing it is more important than using it in all your sentences.
grammar.content.368: Think です = polite and だ = plain.
grammar.content.371: わたし ___ がくせいです。
grammar.content.375: Understand that は marks what we are talking about.
grammar.content.377: は indicates the topic of the sentence.
grammar.content.379: The translation depends on the whole sentence, not on は alone.
grammar.content.381: As a particle, は is pronounced “wa”.
grammar.content.382: Ask yourself: “what are we talking about?”. That item is usually the topic marked with は.
grammar.content.390: The particle か goes at the end of the polite sentence.
grammar.content.391: Turn a polite sentence into a question by adding か at the end.
grammar.content.393: か at the end can turn a polite sentence into a question.
grammar.content.395: You do not need to invert the order as in Spanish.
grammar.content.397: Intonation can help, but the particle already clearly marks the question.
grammar.content.398: In basic polite questions, keep the sentence and add か at the end.
grammar.content.402: Correct. わたしもがくせいです。
grammar.content.404: Use も to indicate that an item shares the same information as another already mentioned.
grammar.content.408: In simple sentences, も takes the place where you would normally put は.
grammar.content.410: It works well when the information is already known.
grammar.content.411: When you want to say “X also…”, think of も first.
grammar.content.420: Connect two nouns to express possession, belonging, origin or a relationship.
grammar.content.422: The first noun describes or relates to the second.
grammar.content.424: It can correspond to “of” or to a possessive relationship.
grammar.content.426: It does not always mean literal ownership.
grammar.content.427: Read A の B as “B related to A”. The specific translation depends on context.
grammar.content.429: The object is near the person listening. What do you use?
grammar.content.434: Correct. それ points to something near the listener.
grammar.content.435: Near the listener, we use それ.
grammar.content.436: Point to objects according to their distance from the speaker and listener.
grammar.content.439: That over there: far from both.
grammar.content.440: これ・それ・あれ can appear alone; they do not need a noun after them.
grammar.content.446: Correct. このほん = this book.
grammar.content.447: Since ほん appears after it, we need この.
grammar.content.448: Point to a specific noun with demonstratives that always need to accompany it.
grammar.content.455: Unlike これ・それ・あれ, この・その・あの need a noun after them.
grammar.content.463: Talk about basic places and ask where something is.
grammar.content.466: There / over there, depending on the distance.
grammar.content.468: The spatial pattern follows the same distance logic as これ・それ・あれ.
grammar.content.470: Which means “I am not a student”?
grammar.content.473: Correct. わたしはがくせいじゃないです。
grammar.content.474: To negate this pattern, we use じゃないです.
grammar.content.475: Negate basic nominal sentences in the polite register and recognize the plain form.
grammar.content.477: じゃないです is common in polite conversation.
grammar.content.479: ではありません is also correct and more formal.
grammar.content.480: じゃない is a very common plain form.
grammar.content.481: Do not memorize three different translations: they all express negation in different registers.
grammar.content.486: がくせいじゃないです。
grammar.content.489: Talk about past nominal states with でした and recognize だった.
grammar.content.491: でした is the polite past of です.
grammar.content.493: だった is the corresponding plain form.
grammar.content.495: The sentence describes a past state.
grammar.content.496: For nouns: です → でした and だ → だった.
grammar.content.498: Which means “I was not a student”?
grammar.content.501: Correct. がくせいじゃなかったです。
grammar.content.502: We need past + negation: じゃなかったです.
grammar.content.503: Combine negation and past in nominal sentences.
grammar.content.505: じゃなかったです expresses the negative past politely.
grammar.content.506: ではありませんでした is a more formal variant.
grammar.content.507: じゃなかった is the plain negative past.
grammar.content.508: Think of two operations: negate + move that negation into the past.
grammar.content.511: We mix です, だ, particles, demonstratives and negative/past forms without telling you which rule applies.
grammar.content.514: Practice mixes concepts because in the exam and in real texts nobody tells you which rule to apply.
grammar.content.522: がくせいです / わたしは
grammar.content.523: がくせいですわたしは。
grammar.content.530: この needs a noun after it.
grammar.content.534: か at the end marks the polite question.
grammar.content.537: A の B expresses a relationship or possession.
grammar.content.542: じゃないです expresses negation.
grammar.content.544: Change it to the polite past.
grammar.content.546: Which expresses “I was not a student”?
grammar.content.547: Negative past: じゃなかったです.
grammar.content.553: これは わたし の ほん です。
grammar.content.557: これ = this, わたしのほん = my book.
grammar.content.559: Describe people, objects, places and states using the two main types of Japanese adjectives.
grammar.content.562: Describe correctly in the present and past, affirmative and negative, and express likes and ability.
grammar.content.565: You should be able to describe people, places and things with い- and な-adjectives, and express likes or basic ability.
grammar.content.601: Start talking about actions, routines and movement with essential verbs and particles.
grammar.content.604: Understand how basic verbs are conjugated and use the main particles in everyday actions.
grammar.content.607: You should be able to describe a simple routine, talk about actions in the present/past and use the main particles fairly confidently.
grammar.content.608: ます / ません / ました
grammar.content.663: Locate people and objects, talk about dates and times and start working with basic quantities.
grammar.content.666: Know how to say where something is, when something happens and understand basic quantity and time expressions.
grammar.content.669: You should be able to describe a room, locate people or objects, read simple schedules and understand basic quantities.
grammar.content.710: Move from basic polite Japanese to the plain forms you will need for more natural structures.
grammar.content.713: Master the essential plain forms and understand how they allow more complex explanations, quotations and modifiers.
grammar.content.717: You should recognize and produce the main plain forms and understand how they are used in longer structures.
grammar.content.718: The progression preserves dependencies: each block uses structures introduced earlier.
grammar.content.719: ない / た / なかった
grammar.content.760: Learn one of the most important building blocks in Japanese for connecting actions, making requests, giving permission and describing states.
grammar.content.763: Form the て-form correctly and use it in the essential patterns of basic Japanese.
grammar.content.766: You should form て confidently and understand its main uses in sequences, states, requests, permission and prohibition.
grammar.content.814: Learn to invite, suggest, request, and express wishes, obligations and advice.
grammar.content.816: Use basic social interaction structures to manage simple conversations.
grammar.content.819: You should be able to invite, suggest, ask for something not to be done, express wishes and understand basic obligations and advice.
grammar.content.858: Move from isolated sentences to more natural messages by connecting reasons, contrasts, lists and time.
grammar.content.860: Build short texts and conversations by linking ideas without relying on completely separate sentences.
grammar.content.863: You should be able to connect several ideas using reasons, contrasts, lists and basic time references.
grammar.content.902: Talk about experiences, plans, comparisons and changes of state with common N5 structures.
grammar.content.904: Express personal experiences, intentions, comparison, change and basic giving and receiving relationships.
grammar.content.907: You should be able to talk about experiences, plans, comparisons and changes, as well as understand giving and receiving.
grammar.content.947: You are no longer studying isolated rules: now you will recognize them together in JLPT-style exercises and texts.
grammar.content.951: Integrate all previous content and practice grammatical recognition and comprehension without hints.
grammar.content.954: This block bridges the gap to full JLPT N5 mock exams and helps identify areas that need review.

grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.subtitle: Japanese step by step
grammar.scorePerfect: Perfect. You recognized all the concepts in Topic {{number}} in this round.
grammar.scoreGood: Very good result. You have a solid foundation; review your mistakes before moving on.

grammar.n5.02.1.title: い-adjectives
grammar.n5.02.1.goal: Describe something and place a description before a noun.
grammar.n5.02.1.rule: い-adjectives have an ending that changes when negating or talking about the past. In the present, they can end a sentence with です or go directly before a noun. Do not add な.
grammar.n5.02.1.example.0: おもしろいです。 — It is interesting.
grammar.n5.02.1.example.1: おもしろいアニメです。 — It is an interesting anime.
grammar.n5.02.1.idea: The same form おもしろい describes something on its own or accompanies a noun.
grammar.n5.02.1.exercise.success: おおきい is an い-adjective: it joins directly to いえ, without な or の.
grammar.n5.02.1.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. おおきい is an い-adjective: it joins directly to いえ, without な or の.
grammar.n5.02.1.preview: おもしろいです。 — It is interesting.
grammar.n5.02.2.title: な-adjectives
grammar.n5.02.2.goal: Distinguish sentence-final descriptions from those accompanying a noun.
grammar.n5.02.2.rule: These adjectives use the copula at the end. な connects the description to the following noun; it does not appear before です. きれい belongs to this group even though it ends in い.
grammar.n5.02.2.example.0: しずかです。 — It is quiet.
grammar.n5.02.2.example.1: しずかなまちです。 — It is a quiet town.
grammar.n5.02.2.idea: な links to a noun: しずかな + まち.
grammar.n5.02.2.exercise.question: Complete “It is a beautiful room”.
grammar.n5.02.2.exercise.prompt: きれい = beautiful · へや = room · きれい＿へやです。
grammar.n5.02.2.exercise.success: きれい is a な-adjective. Before へや it needs な: きれいなへやです。
grammar.n5.02.2.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. きれい is a な-adjective. Before へや it needs な: きれいなへやです。
grammar.n5.02.2.preview: しずかです。 — It is quiet.
grammar.n5.02.3.title: Modifying nouns
grammar.n5.02.3.goal: Choose the correct link for each adjective type.
grammar.n5.02.3.rule: The description comes before what it describes. An い-adjective keeps い; a な-adjective adds な. The noun does not change when it receives a description.
grammar.n5.02.3.example.0: おおきいいえ — a big house.
grammar.n5.02.3.example.1: しずかなへや — a quiet room.
grammar.n5.02.3.idea: い-adjective + noun; な-adjective stem + な + noun.
grammar.n5.02.3.exercise.question: Choose “a new book”.
grammar.n5.02.3.exercise.prompt: あたらしい = new · ほん = book
grammar.n5.02.3.exercise.success: あたらしい belongs to the い group and goes before ほん without adding a link.
grammar.n5.02.3.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. あたらしい belongs to the い group and goes before ほん without adding a link.
grammar.n5.02.3.preview: おおきいいえ — a big house.
grammar.n5.02.4.title: Negative adjectives
grammar.n5.02.4.goal: Negate a description from each group.
grammar.n5.02.4.rule: In the い group, replace the last い with くない. In the な group, use じゃない or ではない. To keep a polite register, you can end these forms with です.
grammar.n5.02.4.example.0: たかくないです。 — It is not expensive.
grammar.n5.02.4.example.1: しずかじゃないです。 — It is not quiet.
grammar.n5.02.4.idea: The い group changes within the adjective; the な group changes the copula.
grammar.n5.02.4.preview: たかくないです。 — It is not expensive.
grammar.n5.02.5.title: Past adjectives
grammar.n5.02.5.rule: For い-adjectives, replace the last い with かった and add です when speaking politely. For な-adjectives, use でした in polite speech or だった in plain form.
grammar.n5.02.5.example.0: あつかったです。 — It was hot.
grammar.n5.02.5.example.1: しずかでした。 — It was quiet.
grammar.n5.02.5.idea: い → かった; な-adjective + でした or だった.
grammar.n5.02.5.exercise.success: おいしい is in the い group: its past is おいしかった. でした is not added to its present form.
grammar.n5.02.5.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. おいしい is in the い group: its past is おいしかった. でした is not added to its present form.
grammar.n5.02.5.preview: あつかったです。 — It was hot.
grammar.n5.02.6.title: Negative past adjectives
grammar.n5.02.6.goal: Say that a description was not true before.
grammar.n5.02.6.rule: In the い group, change くない to くなかった. In the な group, use じゃなかった; the polite variant ではありませんでした is also valid. Here we practice the forms with です.
grammar.n5.02.6.example.0: たかくなかったです。 — It was not expensive.
grammar.n5.02.6.example.1: ひまじゃなかったです。 — I was not free.
grammar.n5.02.6.idea: For い, くなかった; for な, じゃなかった.
grammar.n5.02.6.exercise.question: Choose “It was not fun”.
grammar.n5.02.6.exercise.option.0: たのしくなかったです。
grammar.n5.02.6.exercise.option.1: たのしいじゃなかったです。
grammar.n5.02.6.exercise.success: たのしい → たのしくない → たのしくなかった. The form combines negation and past.
grammar.n5.02.6.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. たのしい → たのしくない → たのしくなかった. The form combines negation and past.
grammar.n5.02.6.preview: たかくなかったです。 — It was not expensive.
grammar.n5.02.7.title: The irregularity of いい
grammar.n5.02.7.goal: Recognize the forms that use the stem よい.
grammar.n5.02.7.rule: いい means good. Its present form is いい, but the changing forms use よ: よくない, よかった and よくなかった. They are not formed with いく or いかった.
grammar.n5.02.7.example.0: いいです。 — It is good.
grammar.n5.02.7.example.1: よくなかったです。 — It was not good.
grammar.n5.02.7.idea: いい keeps いい only in the affirmative present; when changing, it starts from よい.
grammar.n5.02.7.exercise.success: The past of いい is built from よい: よかったです。
grammar.n5.02.7.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The past of いい is built from よい: よかったです。
grammar.n5.02.7.preview: いいです。 — It is good.
grammar.n5.02.8.title: とても・あまり・ぜんぜん
grammar.n5.02.8.goal: Adjust a description without confusing intensity and negation.
grammar.n5.02.8.rule: とても intensifies: very. In the basic Japanese of this course, あまり combines with a negative for “not very”, and ぜんぜん with a negative for “not at all”.
grammar.n5.02.8.example.0: とてもおいしいです。 — It is very tasty.
grammar.n5.02.8.example.1: あまりたかくないです。 — It is not very expensive.
grammar.n5.02.8.idea: とても: very; あまり + negative: not very; ぜんぜん + negative: not at all.
grammar.n5.02.8.preview: とてもおいしいです。 — It is very tasty.
grammar.n5.02.9.title: すき・きらい
grammar.n5.02.9.goal: Express likes with the pattern が + description.
grammar.n5.02.9.rule: すき and きらい act as な-adjectives, although in Spanish we translate them as “like” or “dislike”. Mark what is liked or disliked with が. Do not use を as if they were verbs.
grammar.n5.02.9.example.0: アニメがすきです。 — I like anime.
grammar.n5.02.9.example.1: さかながきらいです。 — I dislike fish.
grammar.n5.02.9.idea: X がすきです / X がきらいです describes your relationship with X.
grammar.n5.02.9.exercise.question: Complete “I like coffee”.
grammar.n5.02.9.exercise.success: コーヒー is what is liked and is marked with が; すき is a description, not a verb with an を object.
grammar.n5.02.9.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. コーヒー is what is liked and is marked with が; すき is a description, not a verb with an を object.
grammar.n5.02.9.preview: アニメがすきです。 — I like anime.
grammar.n5.02.10.title: じょうず・へた
grammar.n5.02.10.rule: じょうず and へた act as な-adjectives. The activity or ability is marked with が. じょうず usually praises another person; avoid using it to boast about your own ability.
grammar.n5.02.10.example.0: たなかさんはうたがじょうずです。 — Tanaka sings well.
grammar.n5.02.10.example.1: わたしはりょうりがへたです。 — I am bad at cooking.
grammar.n5.02.10.idea: Activity がじょうずです / がへたです.
grammar.n5.02.10.exercise.question: Complete “Yuki is good at Japanese”.
grammar.n5.02.10.exercise.prompt: ゆきさんはにほんご＿じょうずです。
grammar.n5.02.10.exercise.success: The ability にほんご is marked with が before じょうず. は introduces the person we are talking about.
grammar.n5.02.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The ability にほんご is marked with が before じょうず. は introduces the person we are talking about.
grammar.n5.02.10.preview: たなかさんはうたがじょうずです。 — Tanaka sings well.
grammar.n5.02.11.title: が with likes and abilities
grammar.n5.02.11.goal: Separate the person from the activity described.
grammar.n5.02.11.example.0: わたしはおちゃがすきです。 — I like tea.
grammar.n5.02.11.example.1: あにはうたがへたです。 — My brother is bad at singing.
grammar.n5.02.11.idea: Person は + thing/activity が + すき・じょうず・へた.
grammar.n5.02.11.preview: わたしはおちゃがすきです。 — I like tea.

grammar.n5.02.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. しんせつ is a な-adjective: add な before ひと.
grammar.n5.02.practice.2.question: Complete “I dislike fish”.
grammar.n5.02.practice.2.prompt: わたしはさかな＿きらいです。
grammar.n5.02.practice.2.success: が marks what is disliked in the pattern with きらい.
grammar.n5.02.practice.2.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. が marks what is disliked in the pattern with きらい.
grammar.n5.02.practice.3.question: Choose “It was fun”.
grammar.n5.02.practice.3.success: The い-adjective forms the past with かった, not with でした.
grammar.n5.02.practice.3.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The い-adjective forms the past with かった, not with でした.
grammar.n5.02.practice.4.question: What does it mean?
grammar.n5.02.practice.4.prompt: ぜんぜんさむくないです。
grammar.n5.02.practice.4.option.1: It is not cold at all.
grammar.n5.02.practice.4.success: ぜんぜん + negative expresses “not at all”; here it is not cold at all.
grammar.n5.02.practice.4.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ぜんぜん + negative expresses “not at all”; here it is not cold at all.
grammar.n5.02.practice.5.question: Choose “It is not good”.
grammar.n5.02.practice.5.success: The changing forms of いい are built from よい: よくない.
grammar.n5.02.practice.5.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The changing forms of いい are built from よい: よくない.
grammar.n5.02.practice.6.question: Complete “My father is bad at singing”.
grammar.n5.02.practice.6.prompt: ちちはうた＿へたです。 · ちち = my father
grammar.n5.02.practice.6.success: The activity うた takes が before へた.
grammar.n5.02.practice.6.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The activity うた takes が before へた.
grammar.n5.02.practice.7.question: Choose “a small dog”.
grammar.n5.02.practice.7.prompt: ちいさい = small · いぬ = dog
grammar.n5.02.practice.7.success: The い-adjective goes directly before the noun.
grammar.n5.02.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The い-adjective goes directly before the noun.
grammar.n5.02.practice.8.question: Choose “I was not free”.
grammar.n5.02.practice.8.option.2: ひまじゃなかったです。
grammar.n5.02.practice.8.success: な-adjectives use the negative past copula: じゃなかった.
grammar.n5.02.practice.8.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. な-adjectives use the negative past copula: じゃなかった.
grammar.n5.02.practice.9.question: What does it mean?
grammar.n5.02.practice.9.prompt: あまりむずかしくないです。
grammar.n5.02.practice.9.option.2: It is not expensive at all.
grammar.n5.02.practice.9.success: あまり with negation softens the description: not very difficult.
grammar.n5.02.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. あまり with negation softens the description: not very difficult.
grammar.n5.03.1.title: What a Japanese verb is
grammar.n5.03.1.goal: Recognize what the verb does at the end of a sentence.
grammar.n5.03.1.rule: The verb usually ends the sentence and expresses an action or state. Its form indicates affirmation or negation and past or non-past. It does not change according to “I”, “you” or “they”.
grammar.n5.03.1.example.0: わたしはたべます。 — I eat.
grammar.n5.03.1.example.1: たなかさんはたべます。 — Tanaka eats.
grammar.n5.03.1.idea: The person does not change the verb; the verb form changes the tense or negation.
grammar.n5.03.1.preview: わたしはたべます。 — I eat.
grammar.n5.03.2.title: Ichidan verbs
grammar.n5.03.2.goal: Recognize a group whose stem is obtained by removing る.
grammar.n5.03.2.rule: For ichidan verbs, remove the final る to form the stem. Many end in an い or え sound + る, but that clue is not enough: learn the group with each verb. かえる, “return”, is godan.
grammar.n5.03.2.example.0: たべる → たべ — eat, stem たべ.
grammar.n5.03.2.example.1: みる → み — see, stem み.
grammar.n5.03.2.idea: Ichidan: keep the word and remove only its final る.
grammar.n5.03.2.exercise.success: おきる is ichidan: removing the final る leaves おき.
grammar.n5.03.2.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. おきる is ichidan: removing the final る leaves おき.
grammar.n5.03.2.preview: たべる → たべ — eat, stem たべ.
grammar.n5.03.3.title: Godan verbs
grammar.n5.03.3.goal: Recognize the endings that change kana row.
grammar.n5.03.3.rule: Godan verbs end in a sound from the う row: う・く・ぐ・す・つ・ぬ・ぶ・む・る. That final sound changes when conjugating. Some godan verbs also end in る: do not remove る as if they were all ichidan.
grammar.n5.03.3.example.0: かく → かき — write, stem for ます.
grammar.n5.03.3.example.1: のむ → のみ — drink, stem for ます.
grammar.n5.03.3.idea: Godan changes the final sound according to the form you need.
grammar.n5.03.3.exercise.question: To prepare ます, which stem does はなす use?
grammar.n5.03.3.exercise.prompt: はなす = speak (godan) · す → し
grammar.n5.03.3.exercise.success: はなす is godan: change す to し and keep the rest, はなし.
grammar.n5.03.3.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. はなす is godan: change す to し and keep the rest, はなし.
grammar.n5.03.3.preview: かく → かき — write, stem for ます.
grammar.n5.03.4.title: する・くる
grammar.n5.03.4.goal: Learn the two basic irregular families.
grammar.n5.03.4.rule: する means do and くる means come. Their forms are learned as pairs: する → します and くる → きます. They do not simply follow the rule of removing る.
grammar.n5.03.4.idea: For these two families, memorize the pair, not a regular rule.
grammar.n5.03.4.exercise.question: Choose the polite form of come.
grammar.n5.03.4.exercise.success: くる is irregular and its polite form is きます.
grammar.n5.03.4.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. くる is irregular and its polite form is きます.
grammar.n5.03.5.title: Dictionary form
grammar.n5.03.5.goal: Understand the non-past value of the entry form.
grammar.n5.03.5.rule: The dictionary form is what you find when looking up a verb. It is an affirmative non-past plain form: depending on context, it expresses a habit or future action. It does not automatically mean “be doing”.
grammar.n5.03.5.example.0: まいにちよむ。 — I read every day.
grammar.n5.03.5.example.1: あしたよむ。 — I will read tomorrow.
grammar.n5.03.5.idea: Context distinguishes habit from future; there is no separate future form.
grammar.n5.03.5.exercise.question: What does this sentence mean in its context?
grammar.n5.03.5.exercise.prompt: あしたはたらく。 · あした = tomorrow · はたらく = work
grammar.n5.03.5.exercise.success: あした places はたらく in the future. The dictionary form is affirmative non-past.
grammar.n5.03.5.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. あした places はたらく in the future. The dictionary form is affirmative non-past.
grammar.n5.03.5.preview: まいにちよむ。 — I read every day.
grammar.n5.03.6.title: ます-form
grammar.n5.03.6.rule: Add ます to the stem: ichidan removes る; godan changes う→い・く→き・ぐ→ぎ・す→し・つ→ち・ぬ→に・ぶ→び・む→み・る→り. する and くる give します and きます. The form is used for habits and future plans.
grammar.n5.03.6.example.0: たべる → たべます — eat.
grammar.n5.03.6.example.1: のむ → のみます — drink.
grammar.n5.03.6.idea: Stem + ます expresses an affirmative action politely.
grammar.n5.03.6.preview: たべる → たべます — eat.
grammar.n5.03.7.title: ません-form
grammar.n5.03.7.rule: The stem is the same as for ます. Replace ます with ません. It expresses that an action does not or will not happen, depending on context.
grammar.n5.03.7.example.0: たべます → たべません — I do not eat.
grammar.n5.03.7.example.1: のみます → のみません — I do not drink.
grammar.n5.03.7.idea: The stem stays the same; ません carries the negation.
grammar.n5.03.7.preview: たべます → たべません — I do not eat.
grammar.n5.03.8.title: ました-form
grammar.n5.03.8.goal: Talk about a past action politely.
grammar.n5.03.8.rule: Keep the stem and replace ます with ました. A marker such as きのう, yesterday, clarifies the time, but the past is already in the verb.
grammar.n5.03.8.example.0: たべます → たべました — I ate.
grammar.n5.03.8.example.1: きのうよみました。 — I read yesterday.
grammar.n5.03.8.idea: Stem + ました expresses affirmative past.
grammar.n5.03.8.preview: たべます → たべました — I ate.
grammar.n5.03.9.title: ませんでした-form
grammar.n5.03.9.goal: Express that an action did not happen.
grammar.n5.03.9.rule: Replace ます with ませんでした without changing the stem. The form combines negation, past and polite speech. It is different from ません, which negates the non-past.
grammar.n5.03.9.example.0: たべませんでした。 — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.03.9.example.1: きのうはたらきませんでした。 — I did not work yesterday.
grammar.n5.03.9.idea: Stem + ませんでした: negated past action.
grammar.n5.03.9.preview: たべませんでした。 — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.03.10.title: を — direct object
grammar.n5.03.10.goal: Mark what directly receives an action.
grammar.n5.03.10.rule: を, pronounced お as a particle, marks the object of verbs such as eat, drink, read or see. It goes after the noun; the verb comes after the object.
grammar.n5.03.10.example.0: パンをたべます。 — I eat bread.
grammar.n5.03.10.example.1: ほんをよみます。 — I read a book.
grammar.n5.03.10.exercise.success: おちゃ is what is drunk, the direct object, and is marked with を.
grammar.n5.03.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. おちゃ is what is drunk, the direct object, and is marked with を.
grammar.n5.03.10.preview: パンをたべます。 — I eat bread.
grammar.n5.03.11.title: に — destination
grammar.n5.03.11.goal: Indicate the place you arrive at.
grammar.n5.03.11.rule: With movement verbs such as いきます, go, に marks the destination. The place name comes before に. This function is different from marking the object with を.
grammar.n5.03.11.example.0: がっこうにいきます。 — I go to school.
grammar.n5.03.11.example.1: うちにかえります。 — I return home.
grammar.n5.03.11.exercise.prompt: えき＿いきます。 · えき = station
grammar.n5.03.11.preview: がっこうにいきます。 — I go to school.
grammar.n5.03.12.title: に — time
grammar.n5.03.12.goal: Mark a specific time without adding に to every time expression.
grammar.n5.03.12.rule: Use に for a specific time or point in time: くじに, at nine. Relative words such as きょう, today, あした, tomorrow, or まいにち, every day, are normally used without に.
grammar.n5.03.12.example.0: くじにおきます。 — I get up at nine.
grammar.n5.03.12.example.1: あしたいきます。 — I will go tomorrow.
grammar.n5.03.12.idea: A specific time takes に; あした and きょう normally do not.
grammar.n5.03.12.exercise.prompt: しちじ＿おきます。 · しちじ = seven in the morning/evening
grammar.n5.03.12.exercise.success: しちじ is a specific time and takes に. Context tells you whether it is morning or evening.
grammar.n5.03.12.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. しちじ is a specific time and takes に. Context tells you whether it is morning or evening.
grammar.n5.03.12.preview: くじにおきます。 — I get up at nine.
grammar.n5.03.13.title: で — place of an action
grammar.n5.03.13.goal: Indicate where an activity takes place.
grammar.n5.03.13.example.0: うちでべんきょうします。 — I study at home.
grammar.n5.03.13.example.1: としょかんでほんをよみます。 — I read at the library.
grammar.n5.03.13.preview: うちでべんきょうします。 — I study at home.
grammar.n5.03.14.title: へ — direction
grammar.n5.03.14.goal: Recognize a direction of movement and its pronunciation.
grammar.n5.03.14.rule: へ is pronounced え as a particle. It marks the direction of a movement. With いきます, you may see に for destination or へ for direction; you do not need to choose between them in a sentence where both fit.
grammar.n5.03.14.example.0: にほんへいきます。 — I go to Japan.
grammar.n5.03.14.example.1: うちへかえります。 — I head back home.
grammar.n5.03.14.idea: The particle is written へ and read え.
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.question: How is the particle in this sentence read?
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.prompt: まちへいきます。 — I go to town.
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.option.0: へ is read as へ, he.
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.option.1: へ is read as え, e.
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.option.2: へ is read as を, o.
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.success: As a direction particle, へ is pronounced え.
grammar.n5.03.14.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. As a direction particle, へ is pronounced え.
grammar.n5.03.14.preview: にほんへいきます。 — I go to Japan.
grammar.n5.03.15.title: と — company
grammar.n5.03.15.goal: Say who you perform an action with.
grammar.n5.03.15.rule: と after a person indicates company. The action is performed with that person. It does not mean destination or place. The same と can also join nouns in a complete list.
grammar.n5.03.15.example.0: ともだちといきます。 — I go with a friend.
grammar.n5.03.15.example.1: あねとたべます。 — I eat with my older sister.
grammar.n5.03.15.exercise.success: たなかさんと expresses company: studying with Tanaka.
grammar.n5.03.15.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. たなかさんと expresses company: studying with Tanaka.
grammar.n5.03.15.preview: ともだちといきます。 — I go with a friend.
grammar.n5.03.16.title: から・まで
grammar.n5.03.16.goal: Indicate a starting point and a limit in space or time.
grammar.n5.03.16.rule: から indicates from where or since when; まで marks how far or until when. They can appear together or separately. Context determines whether the limit is temporal or spatial.
grammar.n5.03.16.example.0: くじからごじまでです。 — It is from nine to five.
grammar.n5.03.16.example.1: うちからえきまでいきます。 — I go from home to the station.
grammar.n5.03.16.idea: から = from; まで = until/to, in this starting-point and limit use.
grammar.n5.03.16.exercise.question: Choose “from ten to three”.
grammar.n5.03.16.exercise.success: じゅうじから marks the start; さんじまで, the end.
grammar.n5.03.16.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. じゅうじから marks the start; さんじまで, the end.
grammar.n5.03.16.preview: くじからごじまでです。 — It is from nine to five.
grammar.n5.03.17.title: ます stem + にいく
grammar.n5.03.17.goal: Express the purpose of going somewhere.
grammar.n5.03.17.rule: Remove ます from the polite form and add にいきます. This stem presents the purpose of the movement. If the action has an object, keep its を in front.
grammar.n5.03.17.example.0: えいがをみにいきます。 — I go to see a film.
grammar.n5.03.17.example.1: パンをかいにいきます。 — I go to buy bread.
grammar.n5.03.17.idea: Action in ます stem + にいきます: go to do something.
grammar.n5.03.17.exercise.prompt: コーヒーを＿にいきます。 · のみます = drink
grammar.n5.03.17.exercise.success: Remove ます from のみます: のみ. コーヒーをのみ にいきます expresses the purpose of going.
grammar.n5.03.17.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Remove ます from のみます: のみ. コーヒーをのみ にいきます expresses the purpose of going.
grammar.n5.03.17.preview: えいがをみにいきます。 — I go to see a film.
grammar.n5.03.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.03.practice.title: Topic 03 review
grammar.n5.03.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.03.practice.0.question: Choose the polite form.
grammar.n5.03.practice.0.success: おきる is ichidan: remove る and add ます.
grammar.n5.03.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. おきる is ichidan: remove る and add ます.
grammar.n5.03.practice.2.question: Choose the polite negative form of do.
grammar.n5.03.practice.2.success: する is irregular: します and, in the negative, しません.
grammar.n5.03.practice.2.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. する is irregular: します and, in the negative, しません.
grammar.n5.03.practice.3.question: Complete “I read the newspaper”.
grammar.n5.03.practice.3.prompt: しんぶん＿よみます。 · しんぶん = newspaper
grammar.n5.03.practice.3.success: The newspaper is the object of reading and takes を.
grammar.n5.03.practice.3.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The newspaper is the object of reading and takes を.
grammar.n5.03.practice.4.question: Complete “I work in a shop”.
grammar.n5.03.practice.4.prompt: みせ＿はたらきます。 · みせ = shop
grammar.n5.03.practice.4.success: で marks the place where working happens.
grammar.n5.03.practice.4.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. で marks the place where working happens.
grammar.n5.03.practice.5.question: Complete “I go to the library”.
grammar.n5.03.practice.5.success: The library is the destination; に fits with いきます.
grammar.n5.03.practice.5.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The library is the destination; に fits with いきます.
grammar.n5.03.practice.6.question: Choose the particles for “I go with my mother at eight”.
grammar.n5.03.practice.6.success: と indicates company and に the specific time.
grammar.n5.03.practice.6.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. と indicates company and に the specific time.
grammar.n5.03.practice.7.question: How is へ pronounced here?
grammar.n5.03.practice.7.success: The direction particle へ is read え.
grammar.n5.03.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The direction particle へ is read え.
grammar.n5.03.practice.8.question: Complete “from school to home”.
grammar.n5.03.practice.8.success: から is the starting point and まで is the limit.
grammar.n5.03.practice.8.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. から is the starting point and まで is the limit.
grammar.n5.03.practice.9.question: Choose “I go to eat sushi”.
grammar.n5.03.practice.9.prompt: すしを＿にいきます。 · たべます = eat
grammar.n5.03.practice.9.success: The purpose of movement uses the ます stem: たべ + にいきます.
grammar.n5.03.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The purpose of movement uses the ます stem: たべ + にいきます.
grammar.n5.04.1.title: あります
grammar.n5.04.1.goal: Express the existence of inanimate things.
grammar.n5.04.1.rule: あります indicates that there is a thing, plant or other entity treated here as inanimate. The existing thing is marked with が. The polite negative is ありません.
grammar.n5.04.1.example.0: ほんがあります。 — There is a book.
grammar.n5.04.1.example.1: じかんがありません。 — I have no time.
grammar.n5.04.1.idea: For things: があります / がありません.
grammar.n5.04.1.exercise.prompt: つくえが＿。 · つくえ = desk
grammar.n5.04.1.exercise.success: A desk is a thing: we use あります for its existence.
grammar.n5.04.1.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. A desk is a thing: we use あります for its existence.
grammar.n5.04.1.preview: ほんがあります。 — There is a book.
grammar.n5.04.2.title: います
grammar.n5.04.2.goal: Express the presence of people and animals.
grammar.n5.04.2.rule: います indicates that there is a person or animal. What exists is marked with が. Its polite negative is いません. Do not use あります for a living person in this basic pattern.
grammar.n5.04.2.example.0: ねこがいます。 — There is a cat.
grammar.n5.04.2.example.1: せんせいがいません。 — The teacher is not here.
grammar.n5.04.2.idea: People and animals: がいます / がいません.
grammar.n5.04.2.exercise.question: Complete “There is a dog”.
grammar.n5.04.2.exercise.success: いぬ, a dog, is an animal: がいます.
grammar.n5.04.2.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. いぬ, a dog, is an animal: がいます.
grammar.n5.04.2.preview: ねこがいます。 — There is a cat.
grammar.n5.04.3.title: が with existence
grammar.n5.04.3.goal: Introduce who or what is there.
grammar.n5.04.3.rule: In a sentence announcing existence, が marks the person or thing that exists. You do not first need to make it the topic with は. In answers to “what is there?”, what exists is identified with が.
grammar.n5.04.3.example.0: こうえんにねこがいます。 — There is a cat in the park.
grammar.n5.04.3.example.1: へやにつくえがあります。 — There is a desk in the room.
grammar.n5.04.3.idea: Place に + existing entity が + あります / います.
grammar.n5.04.3.exercise.prompt: かばんにほん＿あります。
grammar.n5.04.3.exercise.success: ほん is what exists, so it takes が. かばんに indicates its location.
grammar.n5.04.3.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ほん is what exists, so it takes が. かばんに indicates its location.
grammar.n5.04.3.preview: こうえんにねこがいます。 — There is a cat in the park.
grammar.n5.04.4.title: に with existence; contrast with で
grammar.n5.04.4.goal: Distinguish being in a place from acting in that place.
grammar.n5.04.4.rule: With あります and います, に marks where something exists. With an action such as studying, use で. Both can translate as “in”, but their function depends on the verb.
grammar.n5.04.4.example.0: がっこうでべんきょうします。 — I study at school.
grammar.n5.04.4.example.1: がっこうにせんせいがいます。 — There is a teacher at school.
grammar.n5.04.4.idea: に locates existence; で locates an action.
grammar.n5.04.4.exercise.question: Choose the correct particles.
grammar.n5.04.4.exercise.prompt: うち＿いぬがいます。 / うち＿ほんをよみます。
grammar.n5.04.4.exercise.success: The dog is at home: に. Reading is an action performed at home: で.
grammar.n5.04.4.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The dog is at home: に. Reading is an action performed at home: で.
grammar.n5.04.4.preview: がっこうでべんきょうします。 — I study at school.
grammar.n5.04.5.title: Positions
grammar.n5.04.5.goal: Locate something relative to a known object.
grammar.n5.04.5.rule: Use A の + position: うえ above, した below, なか inside, まえ in front, うしろ behind, となり next to. Add に to locate existence. の joins the reference point and the position.
grammar.n5.04.5.example.0: つくえのうえにほんがあります。 — There is a book on the desk.
grammar.n5.04.5.example.1: いえのまえにいぬがいます。 — There is a dog in front of the house.
grammar.n5.04.5.idea: Reference の position に + existing entity が + existence verb.
grammar.n5.04.5.exercise.prompt: いす＿したにねこがいます。 · いす = chair
grammar.n5.04.5.exercise.success: いすのした means “under the chair”. の connects the reference and its position.
grammar.n5.04.5.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. いすのした means “under the chair”. の connects the reference and its position.
grammar.n5.04.5.preview: つくえのうえにほんがあります。 — There is a book on the desk.
grammar.n5.04.6.title: Interrogatives
grammar.n5.04.6.goal: Choose the right question for a person, thing or description.
grammar.n5.04.6.rule: だれ asks who; なに or なん, what; どれ, which one among objects; どの needs a noun and asks which; どんな + noun asks what kind. Use か for a polite question.
grammar.n5.04.6.example.0: これはなんですか。 — What is this?
grammar.n5.04.6.example.1: どのほんですか。 — Which book is it?
grammar.n5.04.6.idea: どれ can stand alone; どの and どんな need a noun.
grammar.n5.04.6.exercise.success: どの accompanies the noun かばん. どれ replaces the noun and cannot be placed like this before it.
grammar.n5.04.6.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. どの accompanies the noun かばん. どれ replaces the noun and cannot be placed like this before it.
grammar.n5.04.6.preview: これはなんですか。 — What is this?
grammar.n5.04.7.title: なにか・なにも
grammar.n5.04.7.rule: なにか expresses something unspecified. なにも with a negative form expresses nothing. なにも does not mean nothing by itself: you need the verb's negation.
grammar.n5.04.7.example.0: なにかありますか。 — Is there anything?
grammar.n5.04.7.example.1: なにもありません。 — There is nothing.
grammar.n5.04.7.idea: なにか: something; なにも + negative: nothing.
grammar.n5.04.7.exercise.success: なにも together with のみません expresses “not drinking anything”.
grammar.n5.04.7.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. なにも together with のみません expresses “not drinking anything”.
grammar.n5.04.7.preview: なにかありますか。 — Is there anything?
grammar.n5.04.8.title: だれか・だれも
grammar.n5.04.8.rule: だれか expresses someone unidentified. だれも with a negative expresses no one. When asking about presence, combine with います; for total absence, with いません.
grammar.n5.04.8.example.0: だれかいますか。 — Is anyone there?
grammar.n5.04.8.example.1: だれもいません。 — There is no one.
grammar.n5.04.8.idea: だれか: someone; だれも + negative: no one.
grammar.n5.04.8.exercise.question: Choose “There is no one in the room”.
grammar.n5.04.8.exercise.success: だれもいません negates the presence of all people. だれかいます says someone is there.
grammar.n5.04.8.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. だれもいません negates the presence of all people. だれかいます says someone is there.
grammar.n5.04.8.preview: だれかいますか。 — Is anyone there?
grammar.n5.04.9.title: Basic counters
grammar.n5.04.9.goal: Count objects and people with the appropriate unit.
grammar.n5.04.9.example.0: りんごがみっつあります。 — There are three apples.
grammar.n5.04.9.example.1: かみがにまいあります。 — There are two sheets of paper.
grammar.n5.04.9.idea: The number combines with an appropriate counter; some readings change.
grammar.n5.04.9.preview: りんごがみっつあります。 — There are three apples.
grammar.n5.04.10.title: Times
grammar.n5.04.10.goal: Read times and ask when during the day.
grammar.n5.04.10.rule: For hours, use じ: いちじ, にじ, さんじ; four is よじ, seven しちじ and nine くじ. For minutes, use ふん or ぷん: ごふん, じゅっぷん. なんじ asks what time. はん means half past.
grammar.n5.04.10.example.0: いま、さんじです。 — It is three o'clock now.
grammar.n5.04.10.example.1: くじはんにおきます。 — I get up at half past nine.
grammar.n5.04.10.idea: Hour + じ; minutes + ふん / ぷん; time of an action + に.
grammar.n5.04.10.exercise.question: What time does this show?
grammar.n5.04.10.exercise.success: よじ is four o'clock; はん adds half an hour.
grammar.n5.04.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. よじ is four o'clock; はん adds half an hour.
grammar.n5.04.10.preview: いま、さんじです。 — It is three o'clock now.
grammar.n5.04.11.title: Days and dates
grammar.n5.04.11.goal: Distinguish day of the week, date and relative references.
grammar.n5.04.11.example.0: きょうはげつようびです。 — Today is Monday.
grammar.n5.04.11.example.1: たんじょうびはしがつみっかです。 — My birthday is April third.
grammar.n5.04.11.idea: Learn weekdays and dates as complete readings; do not invent a date's reading.
grammar.n5.04.11.preview: きょうはげつようびです。 — Today is Monday.
grammar.n5.04.12.title: Duration + くらい・ぐらい
grammar.n5.04.12.rule: じかん expresses hours of duration; じ marks a clock time. Place くらい or ぐらい after the duration to indicate approximately. Do not add に to this basic duration.
grammar.n5.04.12.example.0: にじかんぐらいべんきょうします。 — I study for about two hours.
grammar.n5.04.12.example.1: さんじゅっぷんくらいよみます。 — I read for about thirty minutes.
grammar.n5.04.12.idea: Duration + くらい / ぐらい: approximately that amount of time.
grammar.n5.04.12.preview: にじかんぐらいべんきょうします。 — I study for about two hours.
grammar.n5.04.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.04.practice.title: Topic 04 review
grammar.n5.04.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.04.practice.0.question: Complete “There is a notebook”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.0.success: A notebook is a thing, so あります.
grammar.n5.04.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. A notebook is a thing, so あります.
grammar.n5.04.practice.1.question: Complete “There are children in the park”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.1.prompt: こうえんにこどもが＿。 · こども = children
grammar.n5.04.practice.1.success: People: います; the place is marked with に.
grammar.n5.04.practice.1.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. People: います; the place is marked with に.
grammar.n5.04.practice.2.question: Complete “There is nothing in the bag”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.2.success: なにも with a negative expresses nothing.
grammar.n5.04.practice.2.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. なにも with a negative expresses nothing.
grammar.n5.04.practice.3.question: Complete “There is someone in the house”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.3.success: だれか means someone; います affirms their presence.
grammar.n5.04.practice.3.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. だれか means someone; います affirms their presence.
grammar.n5.04.practice.4.question: Complete “There is a shop next to the station”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.4.prompt: えき＿となりにみせがあります。
grammar.n5.04.practice.4.success: えきのとなり joins the reference and the position.
grammar.n5.04.practice.4.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. えきのとなり joins the reference and the position.
grammar.n5.04.practice.5.question: Choose “What kind of film is it?”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.5.success: どんな asks what kind and accompanies the noun.
grammar.n5.04.practice.5.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. どんな asks what kind and accompanies the noun.
grammar.n5.04.practice.7.question: What does this time mean?
grammar.n5.04.practice.7.success: くじ is nine o'clock and じゅっぷん is ten minutes.
grammar.n5.04.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. くじ is nine o'clock and じゅっぷん is ten minutes.
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.question: Choose “I study for approximately one hour”.
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.prompt: いちじかん = one hour of duration
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.option.0: いちじにべんきょうします。
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.option.1: いちじかんにべんきょうします。
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.option.2: いちじかんくらいべんきょうします。
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.success: The approximate duration is formed with いちじかんくらい, without に.
grammar.n5.04.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The approximate duration is formed with いちじかんくらい, without に.
grammar.n5.05.1.title: ない-form
grammar.n5.05.1.goal: Negate a verb in plain form.
grammar.n5.05.1.rule: Ichidan: remove る and add ない. Godan: change く→か・ぐ→が・す→さ・つ→た・ぬ→な・ぶ→ば・む→ま・る→ら and add ない; う changes to わ. Irregulars: する → しない, くる → こない. ある has the negative ない.
grammar.n5.05.1.example.0: たべる → たべない — not eat.
grammar.n5.05.1.example.1: かう → かわない — not buy.
grammar.n5.05.1.idea: Learn the family first; する and くる are irregular.
grammar.n5.05.1.preview: たべる → たべない — not eat.
grammar.n5.05.2.title: た-form
grammar.n5.05.2.rule: Ichidan: る → た. Godan: う・つ・る → った; む・ぶ・ぬ → んだ; く → いた; ぐ → いだ; す → した. いく → いった is special; する → した and くる → きた are irregular.
grammar.n5.05.2.example.0: たべる → たべた — I ate.
grammar.n5.05.2.example.1: よむ → よんだ — I read (past).
grammar.n5.05.2.idea: The godan past changes by ending group; do not just add た without transforming it.
grammar.n5.05.2.preview: たべる → たべた — I ate.
grammar.n5.05.3.title: なかった-form
grammar.n5.05.3.goal: Negate a verb in the plain past.
grammar.n5.05.3.rule: Start from the negative ない-form and replace its final い with かった. This rule also works with the irregular negatives しない and こない.
grammar.n5.05.3.example.0: たべない → たべなかった — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.05.3.example.1: こない → こなかった — they did not come.
grammar.n5.05.3.idea: Negative ない → なかった: you do not need another godan table for the negative past.
grammar.n5.05.3.preview: たべない → たべなかった — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.05.4.title: Plain form with nouns
grammar.n5.05.4.goal: Use the four copula forms without polite speech.
grammar.n5.05.4.rule: With a noun, だ affirms in the non-past; じゃない negates; だった affirms in the past; じゃなかった negates in the past. The noun stays the same.
grammar.n5.05.4.example.0: がくせいだ。 — I am a student.
grammar.n5.05.4.example.1: がくせいじゃなかった。 — I was not a student.
grammar.n5.05.4.idea: Noun + だ / じゃない / だった / じゃなかった.
grammar.n5.05.4.exercise.success: だった is the affirmative past of the copula in plain form.
grammar.n5.05.4.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. だった is the affirmative past of the copula in plain form.
grammar.n5.05.4.preview: がくせいだ。 — I am a student.
grammar.n5.05.5.title: Plain form of な-adjectives
grammar.n5.05.5.goal: Describe in plain form with the copula pattern.
grammar.n5.05.5.rule: At the end of a sentence, な-adjectives use the same forms as nouns: だ, じゃない, だった, じゃなかった. な only joins the adjective to a noun, not to the copula.
grammar.n5.05.5.example.0: しずかだ。 — It is quiet.
grammar.n5.05.5.example.1: しずかじゃなかった。 — It was not quiet.
grammar.n5.05.5.idea: At the end of the sentence, a な-adjective behaves like a noun with a copula.
grammar.n5.05.5.exercise.question: Choose “I was free” in plain form.
grammar.n5.05.5.exercise.success: ひま is a な-adjective: the plain past uses だった, without な.
grammar.n5.05.5.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ひま is a な-adjective: the plain past uses だった, without な.
grammar.n5.05.5.preview: しずかだ。 — It is quiet.
grammar.n5.05.6.title: Plain form of い-adjectives
grammar.n5.05.6.goal: Recognize the four forms without adding だ.
grammar.n5.05.6.rule: い-adjectives change their own ending: い, くない, かった, くなかった. In plain form they do not need だ. Remember the exception いい → よかった.
grammar.n5.05.6.example.1: あつくなかった。 — It was not hot.
grammar.n5.05.6.idea: An い-adjective ends the sentence with its own form; do not add だ.
grammar.n5.05.6.exercise.success: たかい forms the negative past by changing い to くなかった.
grammar.n5.05.6.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. たかい forms the negative past by changing い to くなかった.
grammar.n5.05.7.title: Polite and plain
grammar.n5.05.7.goal: Connect equivalent forms with different levels of politeness.
grammar.n5.05.7.rule: Polite forms use です and ます; plain forms use the forms you have just learned. They preserve tense and negation, but change the level of politeness. Start with polite forms with strangers; plain forms are also used within longer sentences.
grammar.n5.05.7.example.0: たべます ↔ たべる — eat, affirmative non-past.
grammar.n5.05.7.example.1: たべませんでした ↔ たべなかった — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.05.7.idea: Changing politeness does not change tense or negation.
grammar.n5.05.7.exercise.success: のまなかった keeps the negative and past. のまない does not preserve the past.
grammar.n5.05.7.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. のまなかった keeps the negative and past. のまない does not preserve the past.
grammar.n5.05.7.preview: たべます ↔ たべる — eat, affirmative non-past.
grammar.n5.05.8.title: んです・のです
grammar.n5.05.8.goal: Provide an explanation related to the context.
grammar.n5.05.8.example.0: あした、いくんです。 — The thing is, I am going tomorrow.
grammar.n5.05.8.example.1: いそがしいんです。 — The thing is, I am busy.
grammar.n5.05.8.preview: あした、いくんです。 — The thing is, I am going tomorrow.
grammar.n5.05.9.title: Questions with の？
grammar.n5.05.9.goal: Recognize an explanatory question in informal conversation.
grammar.n5.05.9.rule: In familiar conversation, plain form + の with question intonation can ask for information or an explanation. With a noun or な-adjective in the affirmative non-past, use なの. Do not add it mechanically to every polite question.
grammar.n5.05.9.example.0: あした、いくの？ — Are you going tomorrow?
grammar.n5.05.9.example.1: ひまなの？ — Are you free?
grammar.n5.05.9.idea: Plain form + の？; noun/な-adjective + なの？.
grammar.n5.05.9.exercise.question: Choose the informal question “Are you coming today?”.
grammar.n5.05.9.exercise.prompt: きょう = today · くる = come
grammar.n5.05.9.exercise.success: くる is a verb in plain form: の is added directly, without な.
grammar.n5.05.9.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. くる is a verb in plain form: の is added directly, without な.
grammar.n5.05.9.preview: あした、いくの？ — Are you going tomorrow?
grammar.n5.05.10.title: Quotation with と
grammar.n5.05.10.rule: と after a quotation marks its content before いいます, say. It is not the と of company: here it indicates what is said. Quotation marks make the quote visible.
grammar.n5.05.10.example.1: 「おはよう」といいました。 — They said “good morning”.
grammar.n5.05.10.idea: Quoted words + と + verb of saying.
grammar.n5.05.10.exercise.prompt: 「ありがとう」＿いいます。 — They say “thank you”.
grammar.n5.05.10.exercise.success: と marks the quote ありがとう as what is said.
grammar.n5.05.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. と marks the quote ありがとう as what is said.
grammar.n5.05.11.title: Relative clause + noun
grammar.n5.05.11.goal: Describe a noun with a clause that comes before it.
grammar.n5.05.11.rule: A plain-form clause can directly modify a noun. Place all the information before the noun and do not add a pronoun such as “that”. The tense of the description is preserved.
grammar.n5.05.11.example.0: きのうかったほん — the book I bought yesterday.
grammar.n5.05.11.example.1: まいにちよむほん — the book I read every day.
grammar.n5.05.11.idea: The descriptive clause precedes the noun. Here we focus on plain forms you already know.
grammar.n5.05.11.preview: きのうかったほん — the book I bought yesterday.
grammar.n5.05.12.title: Nominalization with の
grammar.n5.05.12.goal: Turn an action into what you are talking about.
grammar.n5.05.12.rule: Add の to a plain-form verb clause to treat the action as a noun. It can then take が in the likes pattern. This is not the の expressing a relationship between two nouns.
grammar.n5.05.12.example.0: ほんをよむのがすきです。 — I like reading books.
grammar.n5.05.12.example.1: あるくのがすきです。 — I like walking.
grammar.n5.05.12.idea: Verb clause + の forms a unit that can take a particle.
grammar.n5.05.12.exercise.question: Complete “I like listening to music”.
grammar.n5.05.12.exercise.prompt: おんがくをきく＿がすきです。
grammar.n5.05.12.exercise.success: の turns おんがくをきく into the activity that is liked. Then が marks that activity.
grammar.n5.05.12.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. の turns おんがくをきく into the activity that is liked. Then が marks that activity.
grammar.n5.05.12.preview: ほんをよむのがすきです。 — I like reading books.
grammar.n5.05.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.05.practice.title: Topic 05 review
grammar.n5.05.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.05.practice.1.question: Choose the plain past.
grammar.n5.05.practice.1.success: ぶ changes to んだ in the plain past.
grammar.n5.05.practice.1.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ぶ changes to んだ in the plain past.
grammar.n5.05.practice.2.question: Choose “I did not come”.
grammar.n5.05.practice.2.success: くる → こない → こなかった.
grammar.n5.05.practice.2.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. くる → こない → こなかった.
grammar.n5.05.practice.3.question: Choose “I was not a student” in plain form.
grammar.n5.05.practice.3.option.0: がくせいじゃなかった。
grammar.n5.05.practice.3.success: The noun combines with the negative past copula じゃなかった.
grammar.n5.05.practice.3.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The noun combines with the negative past copula じゃなかった.
grammar.n5.05.practice.4.question: Choose “It is beautiful” in plain form.
grammar.n5.05.practice.4.success: きれい is a な-adjective: it uses だ at the end, without な.
grammar.n5.05.practice.4.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. きれい is a な-adjective: it uses だ at the end, without な.
grammar.n5.05.practice.6.question: Choose “Are you a student?” in familiar conversation.
grammar.n5.05.practice.6.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Affirmative non-past noun + なの？.
grammar.n5.05.practice.7.question: Complete the quotation.
grammar.n5.05.practice.7.prompt: 「こんばんは」＿いいました。 — They said “good evening”.
grammar.n5.05.practice.7.success: と marks the quoted words before いいました.
grammar.n5.05.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. と marks the quoted words before いいました.
grammar.n5.05.practice.8.question: Choose “the book I will read tomorrow”.
grammar.n5.05.practice.8.prompt: あした = tomorrow · よむ = read
grammar.n5.05.practice.8.success: The plain clause あしたよむ goes before the noun without の.
grammar.n5.05.practice.8.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The plain clause あしたよむ goes before the noun without の.
grammar.n5.05.practice.9.question: Complete “I like watching films”.
grammar.n5.05.practice.9.prompt: えいがをみる＿がすきです。
grammar.n5.05.practice.9.success: の turns the verb clause into the activity that is liked.
grammar.n5.05.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. の turns the verb clause into the activity that is liked.
grammar.n5.06.1.title: Ichidan → て
grammar.n5.06.1.goal: Obtain the form that connects the verb to other patterns.
grammar.n5.06.1.rule: The て-form does not express past or politeness by itself. For ichidan, replace る with て. The ending that follows determines how the action is used. For する: して; for くる: きて.
grammar.n5.06.1.example.0: たべる → たべて — eat.
grammar.n5.06.1.example.1: みる → みて — to see.
grammar.n5.06.1.idea: Ichidan: remove る and add て; do not confuse て with past た.
grammar.n5.06.1.preview: たべる → たべて — eat.
grammar.n5.06.2.title: Godan う・つ・る → って
grammar.n5.06.2.goal: Group three endings with the same change.
grammar.n5.06.2.rule: For godan ending in う, つ or る, replace that ending with って. Check the group: an ichidan in る uses て, not って. The small っ marks a consonant pause.
grammar.n5.06.2.idea: Godan う・つ・る → って; ichidan る → て.
grammar.n5.06.3.title: Godan む・ぶ・ぬ → んで
grammar.n5.06.3.goal: Recognize the group that ends in んで.
grammar.n5.06.3.rule: Godan in む, ぶ or ぬ replace that whole syllable with んで. The rest of the verb stays the same. The voiced sound で is part of the change, not another particle.
grammar.n5.06.3.example.1: あそぶ → あそんで — play.
grammar.n5.06.4.title: Godan く → いて
grammar.n5.06.4.goal: Change godan in く to いて.
grammar.n5.06.4.rule: For this group, replace く with いて. Keep the rest of the word. いく, go, is an exception you will learn separately: do not extend the regular rule to that verb.
grammar.n5.06.4.example.1: あるく → あるいて — walk.
grammar.n5.06.4.idea: く → いて, with the exception of いく.
grammar.n5.06.5.title: Godan ぐ → いで
grammar.n5.06.5.goal: Preserve the difference between く and ぐ.
grammar.n5.06.5.rule: Godan in ぐ change to いで. Compare with く → いて: voicing distinguishes these two endings. Do not remove the two strokes from で.
grammar.n5.06.5.example.0: およぐ → およいで — swim.
grammar.n5.06.5.example.1: いそぐ → いそいで — hurry.
grammar.n5.06.5.idea: く → いて; ぐ → いで.
grammar.n5.06.5.preview: およぐ → およいで — swim.
grammar.n5.06.6.title: Godan す → して
grammar.n5.06.6.goal: Form the て-form of verbs ending in す.
grammar.n5.06.6.rule: Godan in す change the ending to して. Keep the rest of the word. The irregular する also gives して, but do not confuse its family with the rule for a godan in す.
grammar.n5.06.6.example.0: はなす → はなして — speak.
grammar.n5.06.6.preview: はなす → はなして — speak.
grammar.n5.06.7.title: いく → いって
grammar.n5.06.7.goal: Learn the most common exception in the く group.
grammar.n5.06.7.rule: Although いく ends in く, its て-form is いって. It is the same exception you saw in the past: いった. Memorize the pair to avoid producing いいて.
grammar.n5.06.7.example.0: いく → いって — to go.
grammar.n5.06.7.example.1: いく → いった — I went.
grammar.n5.06.7.idea: いく uses いって and いった.
grammar.n5.06.7.preview: いく → いって — to go.
grammar.n5.06.8.title: Action sequence
grammar.n5.06.8.rule: The て-form links actions. The last verb indicates the tense and politeness of the sequence. You do not need to repeat ます or the past at each step.
grammar.n5.06.8.example.0: おきて、たべます。 — I get up and eat.
grammar.n5.06.8.example.1: ほんをよんで、ねました。 — I read a book and went to bed.
grammar.n5.06.8.idea: Action て、final action: the last verb determines the tense.
grammar.n5.06.8.exercise.success: のんで connects drinking with returning. かえりました at the end places the sequence in the past.
grammar.n5.06.8.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. のんで connects drinking with returning. かえりました at the end places the sequence in the past.
grammar.n5.06.8.preview: おきて、たべます。 — I get up and eat.
grammar.n5.06.9.title: ている — action in progress
grammar.n5.06.9.rule: て-form + います expresses an ongoing action with activity verbs. In plain form it is ている. The context いま, now, helps you understand this use.
grammar.n5.06.9.example.0: いま、ほんをよんでいます。 — I am reading now.
grammar.n5.06.9.example.1: いま、たべています。 — I am eating now.
grammar.n5.06.9.idea: With an ongoing activity, ている describes its progress.
grammar.n5.06.9.exercise.success: きく → きいて + います indicates that listening is happening now.
grammar.n5.06.9.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. きく → きいて + います indicates that listening is happening now.
grammar.n5.06.9.preview: いま、ほんをよんでいます。 — I am reading now.
grammar.n5.06.10.title: ている — resulting state
grammar.n5.06.10.goal: Recognize a state that continues after a change.
grammar.n5.06.10.rule: With some verbs, ている expresses the state that remains after an action. It is not always translated as “be doing”. すんでいます indicates residence; けっこんしています describes being married. Learn each combination with its meaning.
grammar.n5.06.10.example.0: にほんにすんでいます。 — I live in Japan.
grammar.n5.06.10.example.1: あにはけっこんしています。 — My brother is married.
grammar.n5.06.10.idea: ている can show an ongoing activity or a lasting state.
grammar.n5.06.10.exercise.question: What does this sentence usually mean?
grammar.n5.06.10.exercise.prompt: たなかさんはけっこんしています。
grammar.n5.06.10.exercise.success: けっこんしています describes the state of being married, not necessarily an ongoing ceremony.
grammar.n5.06.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. けっこんしています describes the state of being married, not necessarily an ongoing ceremony.
grammar.n5.06.10.preview: にほんにすんでいます。 — I live in Japan.
grammar.n5.06.11.title: てから
grammar.n5.06.11.goal: Indicate that one action is completed first and then another follows.
grammar.n5.06.11.rule: て-form + から indicates that the second action happens after the first. It emphasizes order, rather than just linking actions. The final verb still carries tense and politeness.
grammar.n5.06.11.example.0: たべてから、べんきょうします。 — After eating, I study.
grammar.n5.06.11.example.1: うちにかえってから、ねました。 — I went to bed after returning home.
grammar.n5.06.11.idea: AてからB: first A, then B.
grammar.n5.06.11.preview: たべてから、べんきょうします。 — After eating, I study.
grammar.n5.06.12.title: てください
grammar.n5.06.12.goal: Ask someone to perform an action.
grammar.n5.06.12.rule: Add ください to the て-form to request an action. It is a clear request, but it does not turn any command into a very gentle request; use an appropriate context.
grammar.n5.06.12.example.0: すわってください。 — Sit down, please.
grammar.n5.06.12.example.1: みてください。 — Look, please.
grammar.n5.06.12.idea: て-form + ください requests that the action be done.
grammar.n5.06.12.exercise.prompt: なまえを＿ください。 · かく = write
grammar.n5.06.12.exercise.success: かく changes to かいて; かいてください asks someone to write.
grammar.n5.06.12.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. かく changes to かいて; かいてください asks someone to write.
grammar.n5.06.12.preview: すわってください。 — Sit down, please.
grammar.n5.06.13.title: てもいい
grammar.n5.06.13.goal: Ask for or give permission for an action.
grammar.n5.06.13.rule: て-form + もいいです expresses that doing something is allowed. Add か to ask permission. It is neither an obligation nor a request to perform the action.
grammar.n5.06.13.example.0: ここにすわってもいいですか。 — May I sit here?
grammar.n5.06.13.example.1: たべてもいいです。 — You may eat.
grammar.n5.06.13.idea: てもいい: doing is allowed; てもいいですか asks permission.
grammar.n5.06.13.exercise.success: のむ → のんで, then もいいですか: のんでもいいですか.
grammar.n5.06.13.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. のむ → のんで, then もいいですか: のんでもいいですか.
grammar.n5.06.13.preview: ここにすわってもいいですか。 — May I sit here?
grammar.n5.06.14.title: てはいけない
grammar.n5.06.14.rule: て-form + はいけません expresses that an action is not allowed. The plain form is てはいけない. It does not mean “there is no need”: it forbids the action.
grammar.n5.06.14.example.0: ここでたべてはいけません。 — Eating here is not allowed.
grammar.n5.06.14.example.1: はいってはいけません。 — Entry is not allowed.
grammar.n5.06.14.idea: てはいけない forbids; てもいい permits.
grammar.n5.06.14.exercise.question: What does the notice indicate?
grammar.n5.06.14.exercise.prompt: ここでしゃしんをとってはいけません。 · とる = take a photo
grammar.n5.06.14.exercise.success: てはいけません indicates prohibition: you cannot take photos here.
grammar.n5.06.14.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. てはいけません indicates prohibition: you cannot take photos here.
grammar.n5.06.14.preview: ここでたべてはいけません。 — Eating here is not allowed.
grammar.n5.06.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.06.practice.title: Topic 06 review
grammar.n5.06.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.06.practice.0.question: Choose the て-form.
grammar.n5.06.practice.0.success: Ichidan: remove る and add て.
grammar.n5.06.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Ichidan: remove る and add て.
grammar.n5.06.practice.4.question: Choose the て-forms.
grammar.n5.06.practice.4.prompt: はなす = speak · いく = go
grammar.n5.06.practice.4.success: す → して; いく has the exception いって.
grammar.n5.06.practice.4.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. す → して; いく has the exception いって.
grammar.n5.06.practice.5.question: Choose “I am writing a letter now”.
grammar.n5.06.practice.5.prompt: いま、てがみを＿。 · かく = write
grammar.n5.06.practice.5.success: The ongoing activity uses かいて + います.
grammar.n5.06.practice.5.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The ongoing activity uses かいて + います.
grammar.n5.06.practice.6.question: What does it usually express?
grammar.n5.06.practice.6.prompt: おとうとはとうきょうにすんでいます。 · おとうと = younger brother
grammar.n5.06.practice.6.option.0: My brother is visiting Tokyo just today.
grammar.n5.06.practice.6.success: すんでいます expresses residence, a lasting state.
grammar.n5.06.practice.6.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. すんでいます expresses residence, a lasting state.
grammar.n5.06.practice.7.question: What do they do first?
grammar.n5.06.practice.7.prompt: べんきょうしてから、おちゃをのみます。
grammar.n5.06.practice.7.option.1: Drink and study at the same time.
grammar.n5.06.practice.7.success: してから places studying before drinking tea.
grammar.n5.06.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. してから places studying before drinking tea.
grammar.n5.06.practice.8.question: Complete the request “Open the window”.
grammar.n5.06.practice.8.prompt: まどを＿ください。 · あける = open (ichidan)
grammar.n5.06.practice.8.success: The affirmative request uses the て-form: あけてください.
grammar.n5.06.practice.8.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The affirmative request uses the て-form: あけてください.
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.question: Which message allows the action?
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.prompt: I want to use a room to study.
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.option.0: ここでべんきょうしてはいけません。
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.option.1: ここでべんきょうしてもいいです。
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.option.2: ここでべんきょうしています。
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.success: てもいい gives permission; てはいけません forbids and ています describes an activity.
grammar.n5.06.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. てもいい gives permission; てはいけません forbids and ています describes an activity.
grammar.n5.07.1.title: ませんか — invitation
grammar.n5.07.1.goal: Invite someone to do something with you.
grammar.n5.07.1.rule: ます stem + ませんか can invite politely. Although it contains the negative form, in this context it is not simply a question about a negation.
grammar.n5.07.1.example.0: いっしょにたべませんか。 — Shall we eat together?
grammar.n5.07.1.example.1: えいがをみませんか。 — Would you like to see a film?
